SUMMARY

Caterpillar Inc.(CAT-9.31%)reported record third-quarter sales and an all-time high backlog of $78 billion, supported by demand for power generation and construction equipment. Management stated that capacity constraints in the Power and Energy segment are the primary factor limiting growth, prompting plans to triple large engine production by 2030 through facility repurposing. The Construction Industries segment maintained retail growth for the seventh consecutive quarter, while Resource Industries faced temporary shipping delays in mining operations. The company expects full-year adjusted operating profit margins to be near the bottom of its target range due to strategic investments and higher freight costs.

Operator:Welcome to the Third Quarter 2026 Caterpillar Earnings Conference Call. Please be advised that today's conference is being recorded.[Operator Instructions]I would now like to hand the conference over to your speaker today, Alex Kapper. Thank you. Please go ahead.

Alex Kapper:Thank you, Audra. Good morning, everyone, and welcome to Caterpillar's Third Quarter of 2026 Earnings Call. I'm Alex Kapper, Vice President of Investor Relations. Joining me today are Joe Creed, Chairman and CEO; Kyle Epley, Chief Financial Officer; Stephanie Baughman, Senior Vice President of the Global Finance Services Division; and Ryan Coleman, Senior Director of IR. During our call, we'll be discussing third quarter earnings release we issued earlier today. You can find our slides, the news release and a webcast recap at investors.caterpillar.com under Events and Presentations. The content of this call is protected by U.S. and international copyright law.

Any rebroadcast, retransmission, reproduction or distribution of all or part of this content without Caterpillar's prior written permission is prohibited. Moving to Slide 2. During our call today, we'll make forward-looking statements, which are subject to risks and uncertainties. We'll also make assumptions that could cause our actual results to be different than the information we're sharing with you on this call. Please refer to our recent SEC filings and the forward-looking statements reminder and the news release for details on factors that individually or in aggregate could cause our actual results to vary materially from our forecast.

A detailed discussion of the many factors that we believe may have a material effect on our business on an ongoing basis is contained in our SEC filings. On today's call, we'll also refer to non-GAAP numbers. For any reconciliation of any non-GAAP numbers to the appropriate U.S. GAAP numbers, please see the appendix of the earnings call slides. For today's agenda, Joe will begin by sharing his perspectives about our results, and he will highlight key initiatives across our segments. Then he'll discuss our full year outlook and insights about our end markets. Kyle will provide a detailed overview of results and share key assumptions looking forward. We will conclude by taking your questions.

Now let's advance to Slide 3 and turn the call over to Joe Creed.

Joseph Creed:All right. Good morning, and thanks, Alex. I appreciate everyone joining us today. Our third quarter results reflect the durability of our end markets with our highest sales quarter ever, strong order rates and a record backlog. Our team continues to execute our strategic priorities in a dynamic environment, positioning us for a strong year. Sales and revenues were $20.7 billion, up 17% versus the prior year, driven by strong end market demand. We delivered adjusted profit per share of $7.20, an increase of 45% versus last year. Strong order rates across all 3 of our primary segments drove backlog to a record $78 billion.

That's an increase of approximately $38 billion or 96% from the third quarter last year and marks the fourth consecutive quarter of sequential backlog growth in all 3 of our primary segments. The quarter demonstrated the team's ability to execute in a high-growth environment. Specifically, our Power and Energy team continued to increase production of large reciprocating engines and turbines while simultaneously expanding capacity to meet demand. The team is effectively managing the operational challenges that come with this rapid growth, bringing additional capacity online is still the top pacing factor for growth in Power and Energy. So working diligently to execute our plans and meet our customers' needs.

As I mentioned, sales and revenues were $20.7 billion, and they were in line with our expectations. The increase from the prior year was primarily driven by strong growth in sales volume and favorable price realization in all 3 of our primary segments. Third quarter adjusted operating profit margin was 20.6%. Excluding IEEPA tariff recoveries, adjusted operating profit margin was in line with our expectations. In the third quarter, we generated MP&E free cash flow of $3.8 billion and deployed $2 billion to shareholders through share repurchases and dividends. Now I'll review third quarter retail statistics. In Power and Energy, sales to users grew a robust 36%.

Power generation grew 75%, driven by continued very strong demand for turbines and large reciprocating engines used in data center applications. Sales to users in oil and gas increased 5% and were driven by turbines and turbine-related services. Industrial sales to users were down due to softness in the EAME region. Now for Construction Industries. We have one of the broadest ranges of products, technology and services to support customers whether they prefer to own lease or rent equipment. Combined with healthy construction activity, our unique position has allowed us to outpace the industry throughout the year. In the third quarter, total sales to users increased 20%, marking the seventh consecutive quarter of year-over-year growth.

In North America, sales to users grew a robust 27%, in line with our expectations. Dealer rental revenue in North America continued to grow, driving increased investment in their equipment fleets. We also saw strong customer interest in the Cat dealer-owned rental joint venture called Major Projects, which was launched last quarter. As a reminder, Major Projects will serve customers developing large-scale infrastructure across North America, including transportation, energy, manufacturing and data center builds. It's a supplemental national rental solution to help deliver larger size class construction equipment and capabilities where existing individual dealer rental fleets aren't sufficient to execute at scale.

As a result, rental fleet loading was exceptionally strong in the third quarter, contributing significantly to sales to users growth compared with prior year when fleet loading was a slight headwind. Even excluding the positive impact from the rental fleet loading, sales to users growth was strong, driven by residential and nonresidential construction activity. Sales to users in EAME were above expectations with growth driven by strength in Europe and Africa, partially offset by softness in the Middle East. In Asia Pacific, sales to users outside of China were lower than we anticipated and declined slightly due to timing. China, however, continued to grow from a low base as we expected.

Latin America continued to grow but at a lower rate than we anticipated. For Resource Industries, third quarter sales to users increased 4%, which is below our expectations. Sales to users were higher in heavy construction, quarry and aggregates, but lower in mining due to delays in shipping and commissioning. The rail decrease was driven by lower international locomotive deliveries. Turning to Slide 4. I'll cover a few highlights since our last earnings call, starting with Power and Energy. We serve customers across the power and energy value chain and demand for our solutions remains strong. To ensure we can meet their needs and maintain operational excellence, we're continually evaluating opportunities to repurpose underutilized facilities across our footprint.

In line with that approach, we plan to use a portion of our Winston-Salem, North Carolina facility, which currently produces locomotive engines as a second assembly and test location for the 3600 series large reciprocating engine. The footprint will support our oil and gas customers to meet the growing need for natural gas compression. The initiative directly supports previously announced plans to increase large reciprocating engine capacity to nearly 3x to the '24 level by 2030. Utilizing our existing footprint and workforce is the most cost-effective and quickest way for us to bring additional capacity online.

In Construction Industries, we launched Cat Compact earlier this year, a key part of our strategy to reach more small contractors in the growing compact construction equipment industry. To support that growth and meet increasing customer demand, we announced a $1 billion investment to expand manufacturing capacity in Sanford, North Carolina. The investment will create a modern technology-enabled manufacturing environment designed to improve safety, quality and operational performance while supporting long-term growth. The facility will incorporate advanced manufacturing technologies, automation, digital production systems and integrated logistics capabilities to create a more connected and efficient operation. This demonstrates how we're aligning our investments to meet our 2030 targets and positioning Caterpillar for long-term profitable growth.

And in Resource Industries, we announced last month that we're working with Luck Stone to expand autonomous hauling technology across 2 additional Virginia operations. The expansion follows a highly successful pilot at the Bull Run quarry where autonomous trucks have hauled more than 3.5 million tons since going live in November of 2024. These deployments also marked the first use of Caterpillar's autonomous technology on a Cat 775 truck, expanding our advanced autonomy capabilities beyond large mining applications and into quarry and aggregates. Through this customer collaboration, we gained insights that are helping us refine and scale our autonomous hauling solutions to deliver measurable value for operations at job sites around the world.

This expansion marks another important step towards our goal of tripling the number of Cat autonomous trucks by 2030 compared with 2024. Now on Slide 5, I'll provide an update on our outlook. Our strong execution through the first 9 months positions us well to meet our full year outlook. We continue to expect our full year 2026 sales and revenues to grow in the mid- to high teens. Strong order rates and a growing backlog reflect continued broad-based momentum across our business despite ongoing geopolitical uncertainty. Excluding the favorable impact from IEEPA tariff recoveries, we continue to expect full year adjusted operating profit margin to be near the bottom of the target range.

Our full year margin expectation reflects the strategic investments we're making to execute our growth strategy as well as the ongoing impact of tariffs and higher freight costs due to elevated energy prices. We remain focused on delivering long-term OPACC growth, and we aim to operate around the midpoint of our adjusted operating profit margin target range over time. We're also maintaining our MP&E free cash flow expectations to be in the top half of our annual target range. Kyle will provide additional details to you shortly. And now I'll discuss our key end markets, starting with Power and Energy. We continue to work closely with our customers, which allows us to understand and respond to their evolving needs.

Customers view of demand for both oil and gas and power generation remains strong. As I mentioned, backlog continues to grow due to strong order rates, and we're now taking some large reciprocating orders as far out as 2029 and turbine orders into 2030. We continue to anticipate full year growth in power generation for both Cat reciprocating engines and Solar Turbines driven by increasing energy demand to support the data center build-out related to cloud computing and generative AI. Additionally, prime power demand continues to trend higher as customers look to Caterpillar's turbine and reciprocating engine products to support their need for power solutions.

After a record year for sales in 2025, oil and gas is expected to grow moderately again this year. Reciprocating engine sales are anticipated to increase driven by strong demand in gas compression applications. We also see continued momentum in demand for reciprocating engine aftermarket parts. Solar Turbines oil and gas sales are expected to grow and the backlog remains healthy with solid order and inquiry activity. Demand for products and industrial applications is expected to grow moderately in 2026 as well. For Construction Industries, we expect strong fourth quarter and full year sales to users growth, supported by healthy end markets. The outlook for North America remains positive with construction spending at healthy levels.

Nonresidential construction investment continues to be supported by the IIJA, critical infrastructure programs and data centers. We expect fourth quarter dealer rental fleet loading to remain strong. However, it will contribute less to sales to users growth than in the third quarter due to lapping strong rental loading in the fourth quarter of last year. In EAME, Europe is expected to remain stable, supported by nonresidential construction, while construction activity in Africa is projected to remain strong. The Middle East continues to face challenges, and we currently anticipate only a limited impact on EAME sales to users. In Asia Pacific, outside of China, stable economic conditions are expected.

In China, we anticipate moderate conditions with full year growth in the above 10-ton excavator industry off low levels of activity. We expect full year growth in Latin America. We're seeing continued positive momentum in Resource Industries with robust order rates driving strong backlog growth. Customer product utilization is high and the age of the fleet remains elevated. Most key commodities remain above investment thresholds and customers are focused on the long term. For full year 2026, we expect strong sales to users growth, primarily driven by rising demand for copper and gold, increasing activity in the Canadian oil sands and positive dynamics in heavy construction and quarry and aggregates.

We expect commissioning delays from the third quarter to catch up, which will contribute to strong sales to users growth in the fourth quarter. We continue to expect rebuild activity to increase moderately compared with last year. Rail services are anticipated to grow for the year, and we now see -- we now expect locomotive deliveries to be slightly lower year-over-year due to timing of deliveries. And finally, earlier this month, we announced that Derrick York will succeed Denise Johnson as Group President of Resource Industries. I want to congratulate Denise on a remarkable career. Under her leadership, Resource Industries returned to profitability and positioned Caterpillar as an industry leader in mining, autonomy and technology.

I'm deeply grateful for all she's done to strengthen our relationships with customers, develop our people and shape the future of our company. Her impact and influence will be remembered long after her retirement. I've worked closely with Derrick for well over a decade. And I'm confident in his ability to lead the RI team into its next chapter of innovation, growth and customer success. He is a highly respected leader who understands our customers, our strategy and the industries that we serve. With that, I'll turn it over to Kyle.

Kyle Epley:Thank you, Joe. Good morning, everyone. I'm going to take a few minutes to walk you through our third quarter results, including details about segment performance as well as the balance sheet and cash flow. I will finish with remarks on our expectations for the fourth quarter and current full year assumptions. Beginning on Slide 6. Sales and revenues were $20.7 billion, up 17% versus the prior year, which was in line with our expectations. Adjusted operating profit was $4.3 billion, and our adjusted operating profit margin was 20.6%. Excluding the IEEPA tariff recoveries, both were in line with expectations.

Moving to Slide 7, the 17% increase in sales and revenues compared to the third quarter of 2025 was primarily driven by strong growth in sales volume and favorable price realization. The stronger sales volume was mainly driven by higher sales of equipment to end users, supported by healthy end market demand and strong execution by our team. Dealer inventory increased by $300 million in Construction Industries compared to an increase of $600 million in the third quarter of 2025. This created a modest headwind to sales volume in the quarter and was in line with our expectations. Sales and revenues both at a consolidated level and across all 3 primary segments were in line with our expectations.

Moving to operating profit on Slide 8. Operating profit in the third quarter increased by 38% to $4.2 billion, adjusted operating profit of $4.3 billion also increased by 38% versus the prior year. The adjusted operating profit margin was 20.6%, which was an increase of 310 basis points compared to the prior year. The margin benefited from the profit impact of higher sales volume and favorable price realization. This was partially offset by higher manufacturing costs, mainly driven by higher freight and higher expenses related to our capacity expansions. In the quarter, we recognized $128 million in IEEPA tariff recoveries. Nearly all this amount is reflected in corporate items.

For tariffs introduced since the beginning of 2025 and excluding IEEPA recoveries, our third quarter tariff costs were approximately $600 million and about flat year-over-year as we anticipated. Moving to Slide 9. Profit per share was $7.13 in the quarter. Adjusted profit per share was $7.20. Excluding discrete items, the provision for income taxes in the third quarter of 2026 reflected a global estimated annual effective tax rate of 23%. Finally, the year-over-year impact from the reduction in the average number of shares outstanding due to share repurchases resulted in a favorable impact on adjusted profit per share of approximately $0.15 compared to the third quarter of 2025.

On Slide 10, I will now review the third quarter results of our segments, starting with Power and Energy. For Power and Energy, sales of $8.8 billion increased by 18% versus the prior year, which was in line with our expectations. The sales increase versus the prior year was mainly due to higher sales volume and favorable price realization. Services revenues were also strong in the quarter, especially for sales into oil and gas applications. Third quarter profit for Power and Energy increased by 31% versus the prior year to $2.1 billion. The segment's margin of 24.4% was an increase of 250 basis points versus the prior year.

The increase was mainly due to the profit impact of higher sales volume. Favorable price realization was mostly offset by unfavorable manufacturing costs driven by spend related to our capacity expansions, including higher depreciation along with higher freight and material costs. Segment margins matched our expectations. Now moving to Slide 11. Construction Industries sales increased by 18% in the third quarter to $8 billion as we anticipated. The sales increase versus the prior year was primarily due to the higher sales volume and favorable price realization. Higher sales volume was mainly driven by sales of equipment to end users, which included strong contributions from both retail sales and rental fleet loading. Both residential and nonresidential industries contributed to the growth.

Third quarter profit for Construction Industries was $1.8 billion, a 33% increase versus the prior year. The segment's margin of 22.9% was an increase of 250 basis points versus the prior year, mainly driven by favorable price realization and the profit impact of higher sales volume. This was partially offset by unfavorable manufacturing costs, including the impact of freight and tariff costs. SG&A and R&D expenses related to our digital and technology investments also increased compared to the prior year. Segment margin was also consistent with our expectations. Turning to Slide 12. Resource Industries sales, which were broadly in line with our expectations increased by 15% in the third quarter to $4.6 billion, primarily driven by higher sales volume.

Price realization was also favorable versus the prior year and slightly better than our expectations primarily driven by positive geographic mix. Third quarter profit for Resource Industries increased by 14% versus the prior year to $622 million. The segment's margin of 13.5% was roughly unchanged versus the prior year. This was mainly driven by unfavorable manufacturing costs, primarily due to higher material costs, including tariffs, offset by the profit impact of higher sales volume and favorable price realization. Overall, the segment margin was about in line with our expectations. Moving to Slide 13. Financial Products revenues increased by 9% versus the prior year to $1.2 billion, mainly due to higher average earning assets across all regions.

Segment profit increased by 10% to $264 million. This increase was primarily due to a favorable impact from higher average earning assets, partially offset by a higher provision for credit losses. Our customers' financial health remains strong. Past dues were 1.31% in the quarter, down 16 basis points versus the prior year and remains the lowest level we have recorded since 1998. The allowance rate was 0.91% at the end of the third quarter. Business activity within Cat Financial remains healthy. Retail new business volume grew by 6% versus the prior year.

In addition, used equipment inventory levels continue to remain low and conversion rates remain above historical averages as customers continue to choose to purchase their equipment at the end of their lease term. Moving on to Slide 14. MP&E free cash flow was $3.8 billion in the quarter. This was an increase of roughly $600 million versus the prior year, mainly driven by stronger profit. CapEx spend was about $700 million in the quarter. We deployed $2 billion to shareholders in the third quarter, of which share repurchases accounted for $1.2 billion and nearly $750 million for our quarterly dividend payment.

Earlier this year, we announced our sixth consecutive year of high single-digit quarterly dividend increase and this year will mark 33 consecutive years of paying higher annual dividends to our shareholders. Our balance sheet remains strong. We have ample liquidity with an enterprise cash balance of $7.9 billion. In addition, there is $1.6 billion in slightly longer-dated liquid marketable securities to improve yields on our cash. Now for outlook assumptions. Turning to Slide 15. I will start with the fourth quarter. End user demand remains favorable across all 3 primary segments and the team is working diligently to deliver on our commitments for the year.

At the same time, we are aware of potential headwinds presented by higher cost inflation, which we continue to monitor closely. For the fourth quarter, we anticipate moderate sales growth versus the prior year. As a reminder, we are lapping a strong quarter last year, which creates a tougher comparison this year. Now let me walk you through each of our 3 primary segments. In Power and Energy, we anticipate moderate sales growth in the fourth quarter versus the prior year as we lap a strong prior year fourth quarter and continue to ramp capacity.

Volume growth is expected to be driven by continued strength in power generation, modest growth in oil and gas and moderate growth in industrial applications as it continues to recover. We also expect favorable price realization. In Construction Industries, we expect sales to be similar to the prior year. We anticipate the typical seasonal dealer inventory reduction to be roughly $1.6 billion, which compares to a decline of $600 million in the fourth quarter of 2025. As a result, we expect the year-over-year impact to be about a $1 billion headwind to sales volume in the fourth quarter against the backdrop of continued strong sales to users and industry growth.

As a result, we expect sales volume in Construction Industries to be down modestly versus the prior year. However, we continue to expect favorable price realization in the fourth quarter. Despite the drawdown, we continue to expect dealer inventories at the end of the year to be higher than the prior year in anticipation of strong sales to users in 2027. In Resource Industries, we expect strong sales growth in the fourth quarter versus the prior year. Volume is expected to be driven by higher sales to users and services growth. We also anticipate favorable price realization. I will now provide some color on our fourth quarter margin expectations versus the prior year.

At the enterprise level, we expect higher adjusted operating profit margin versus the prior year. This is primarily due to a favorable price realization and the profit impact of higher sales volume. Excluding the impact of lower tariffs, we expect unfavorable manufacturing costs driven by higher freight as well as expenses related to our capacity expansions. SG&A and R&D expenses are also expected to be higher, driven by our continued investment in the strategic initiatives aligned with our 2030 goals. We anticipate tariff costs, excluding IEEPA recoveries of around $600 million, which is similar to what we incurred in the third quarter, but roughly $200 million lower than what we incurred in the fourth quarter of 2025.

We continue to expect about 50% of the tariffs to be incurred in Construction Industries and 25% in both Power and Energy and Resource Industries. Now for our fourth quarter margin expectations in our 3 primary segments. In Power and Energy, we anticipate favorable price realization and stronger volume to drive a higher margin percentage compared to the prior year. The higher margin compared to the prior year is expected to be partially offset by unfavorable manufacturing costs, including depreciation and expenses related to our capacity expansion, along with higher material and freight costs. We expect fourth quarter margin to be similar to the third quarter.

In Construction Industries, we anticipate a higher margin percentage compared to the prior year, primarily due to the favorable price realization, which is partially offset by lower sales volume. Excluding the impact of lower tariffs, manufacturing costs are expected to be higher, driven by freight. We also expect higher SG&A and R&D related to our technology investments. Also, as a reminder, our Construction Industries fourth quarter margin typically has a sequential step down from the third quarter. We expect this seasonality change to be slightly more than our typical average step down due to the expected lower sales volume, higher SG&A and R&D related to our technology and digital investments as well as higher freight costs.

In Resource Industries, we anticipate a higher margin percentage compared to the prior year, driven by favorable price realization and the profit impact of higher sales volume, partially offset by unfavorable manufacturing cost including freight and material. Now on Slide 16, let me provide a few comments on the full year. As Joe mentioned, we continue to anticipate sales and revenues growth in the mid- to high teens for the full year 2026.

Our strong full year sales and revenues expectations is supported by strong sales to users growth across all 3 primary segments driven by healthy end markets, strong order rates across all 3 primary segments driving our backlog growth, increased output from our capacity expansion plans, which remain on schedule, and a strong year of services growth. Now for our adjusted operating profit margin for the full year. Compared to last year, we expect a higher adjusted operating profit margin, which reflects profit impact of higher sales and favorable price realization, partially offset by unfavorable manufacturing costs, including spend related to our capacity expansion, which includes higher depreciation expense as well as higher freight. We also expect higher SG&A and R&D.

Excluding IEEPA tariff recoveries, our full year adjusted operating profit margin is expected to be near the bottom of our target range. Excluding our reported year-to-date IEEPA tariff recoveries of about $520 million, we continue to expect full year 2026 tariff costs of around $2.2 billion. Our outlook does not include any additional IEEPA tariff recoveries in the fourth quarter. We now expect restructuring costs of about $300 million in 2026, which is on the low end of our prior range. Our estimated global annual effective tax rate remains approximately 23% for 2026, excluding discrete items.

We also continue to expect MP&E free cash flow to be in the top half of our annual target range of $6 billion to $15 billion. Our CapEx spend for 2026 is now anticipated to be about $3.3 billion, which is slightly below our prior expectations of $3.5 billion. Now turning to Slide 17 to summarize. We delivered another very strong quarter with year-to-date financial results tracking toward another record year for Caterpillar. Our end markets remain healthy with strong order rates and a growing backlog, we continue to drive improved profitability in a dynamic operating environment. We will remain disciplined and committed to operational excellence and the O&E model. We will continue to look for ways to invest efficiently.

We will maintain a strong balance sheet and continue to return substantially all of our MP&E free cash flow to our shareholders through dividends and share repurchases over time. And finally, we will continue to execute our strategy for profitable growth. With that, we will take your questions.

Operator:[Operator Instructions]Your first question comes from the line of Tami Zakaria from JPMorgan. Hearing no response, we'll go next to Rob Wertheimer with Melius Research.

Robert Wertheimer:I had a couple of questions around Power Gen. And 2 quarters ago, you detailed some of the Prime Power projects you've done, I think you gave gigawatt numbers. Do you have any update there? Is Prime Power still expanding for you, either in general, if you have any update on gigawatts. And then you mentioned you're taking orders into '29. Does that imply that '28 is sold out? Are you selling out current capacity but leaving future capacity for future orders? Can you just sort of talk about how you manage backlog there?

Joseph Creed:Rob, we still continue to see trending higher Prime Power, both turbines and reciprocating gen sets. I've had a handful of discussions with customers for Prime Power just in this last quarter. So a lot of quoting activity continuing to go on. And I think we'll continue to see that trend as we move into the future. We're not seeing anything different in that space. When it comes to orders and sort of backlog, if it's significant order in gas, Prime Power, we're probably looking at 2029. I mean maybe some -- we'll probably still roll some diesel backup orders into 2028, we're not completely full.

But we're still -- we have frame agreements in the pipeline that kind of convert to orders as we move over time. So again, we continue to have extended backlog. I'm happy that the backlog grew in all 3 segments. And what we're hearing from our customers is they still want more from us if we can get them more power. So we're trying to ramp as quickly as we can and still hit our customers' needs.

Operator:We'll go next to Tami Zakaria at JPMorgan.

Tami Zakaria:Good morning. Can you hear me?

Joseph Creed:We can.

Tami Zakaria:So just wanted to touch on that backlog comment. I think I heard you say that the engines and turbine orders are now going as far as 2029, 2030. So is it that the total orders you received in the quarter are primarily for the out years? Or are the majority of the orders booked still for the next 12 months. And given the new capacity that will be coming online, when would you expect this record backlog to start stepping down? Or is it the new normal for the backlog magnitude?

Joseph Creed:Tami, thanks for the question. So I want to be clear, I mean, we're taking our orders into '29. We have some in '29 and 2030, we still have more to fill. And this is a bit of a complicated question because it's going to depend on the product, right? So for a large reciprocating engines and turbines, we're definitely extended out into late '28 into '29. Smaller gensets, smaller engines, obviously, lead times are much shorter than that. And on the machine side of the business, the backlog grew in all 3 segments, aside from a couple of products where we're ramping production and operationally trying to ramp production and even those were not extended near as far.

I would like to produce and get our production ramp closer to STU. So when we look at the backlog, we want to make sure we're looking at the backlog in the context of sales to users and order rates and the entire system and how it works. So if we can -- sales to users stay healthy, which is what we're expecting, and we can produce more product, we'll continue to take orders, but I would like to see the backlog -- I mean if we can get it to even come in on the machine side because we can keep up, that would be a good thing.

And I also think if you -- when you look at, we've had a few quarters of backlog growth, I think we'll continue to see some backlog growth, but it's going to really depend. I mean customers have time to place orders and sort of digest what we have. And so I don't know that quarter-to-quarter, it's going to be something we look at as the singular metric as we start to move out, especially as we get extended. We're continuing to do long-term planning with our big data center customers and Prime Power customers. We're seeing demand for cloud compute and our backup power continue to be strong.

And then AI obviously comes in on top of that in the Prime Power numbers. So with those frame agreements, we have a line of sight past the backlog, and we continue to talk to our customers. And then on Prime Power, those are big projects. And I think they get negotiated individually and those can come in lumpy in the backlog as can mining orders. So I'm really pleased with the backlog growth we saw in this quarter. It was broad-based. Oil and gas, power gen, RI, and CI. So we have good momentum.

Kyle Epley:And just for a reference, we expect 58% of our backlog is expected to be sold within the next 12 months and that's comparative to 59% last quarter.

Operator:We'll move next to Jamie Cook at Truist Securities.

Jamie Cook:I guess my question, Joe, is just around your longer-term margin framework that you guys have put out there. You guys have done an exceptional job, but the margins have been pushing towards the lower end. Obviously, we have tariffs and inflationary pressures, et cetera. But like what do you think with sort of capacity coming online and price cost in your backlog, what's like a reasonable time for us to assume we can get back towards like the mid- to high end of your longer-term target range, and what would be the major drivers behind that?

And then last, is there any way you can help us frame how much incremental capacity is coming online in 2027 on a dollar basis if or any way you could frame it.

Joseph Creed:Jamie. As far as the margin target range, we -- I've said many times, I want to operate towards the middle of that range. The sales are growing at a really good clip, which is a good thing, and we've been able to, as best we can keep up with customer demand, and it's a progressive target. So as our margins are going up, the target continues to increase. So we're kind of skipping along the bottom.

I would expect and we'll talk to you a lot more about 2027 in the next quarter that we start to claw our way off the bottom of that margin target range as we go forward, while we still try to keep up with demand. We also are trying to do this with the tariff headwind in a smart way where we're not slowing down investments that would impact the growth and the momentum we have in the business. So I'm happy with the progress we've made, our margins continue to go up as our volume goes up and over the next couple of years, we want to try to work our way back to the midpoint.

Operator:Next, we'll move to David Raso at Evercore ISI.

David Raso:I'm trying to figure out the revenue sequentially and what it means when we think about '27 revenue. If you look at the sequential revenue 3Q to 4Q, let's use the guide for the full year, mid- to high teens, right, let's call it, 17%. It implies the fourth quarter, even if I give you back the extra $1 billion, right, the headwind of the dealer inventory, it implies the revenue is barely up sequentially. And over a long period of time, fourth quarter is up 5% to 10%. I mean it moves around, but a year where you're adding capacity, it's a big focus. And I mean demand is there.

You speak to in retail, even the backlog is still pretty solid. Just trying to understand, is there some capacity issue, supplier issue, why is the revenue growth so modest sequentially especially given the capacity adds? And any implications on how to think about '27 top line would be appreciated as well.
